public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Fibonacci Primes

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_prime)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace FibonacciPrimes

/--
There are infinitely many Fibonacci primes, i.e., Fibonacci numbers that are prime
It is also a barrier to defining a benchmark from this paper:
https://arxiv.org/html/2505.13938v1 (see Figure 8).

-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem fib_primes_infinite : {n : ℕ | (∃ m : ℕ, m.fib = n) ∧ n.Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many indices $i$, such that the $i$-th Fibonacci is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem fib_primes_infinite.variant : {n : ℕ | n.fib.Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
The two ways of phrasing the conjecture are equivalent.
-/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem indices_infinite_iff_fib_primes_infinite : type_of% fib_primes_infinite.variant ↔
    type_of% fib_primes_infinite := by
  simp only [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  constructor
  · intros h a
    rcases h (a + 1) with ⟨b', ⟨hb₁, hb₂⟩⟩
    use Nat.fib b'
    exact ⟨⟨exists_apply_eq_apply Nat.fib b', hb₁⟩,
      by linear_combination b'.le_fib_add_one + hb₂⟩
  · intro h a
    rcases h (Nat.fib a) with ⟨b', ⟨⟨m, hm⟩, hb₁⟩, hb₂⟩
    use m
    constructor
    · simp_all
    · have := @m.fib_mono a
      omega

end FibonacciPrimes

reformulations.difference: States infinitude of indices n for which Nat.fib n is prime, rather than infinitude of distinct Fibonacci prime values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The value set is exactly the image under Nat.fib of the qualifying index set. Prime-producing indices are at least 3, and Nat.fib is strictly increasing on indices at least 2, so this map is a bijection between the two sets. Consequently their infinitude is equivalent. An independent proof of the biconditional compiled in /workspace/review/scratch.lean using the growth bound n ≤ Nat.fib n + 1 and monotonicity; it has no sorryAx dependency.

Boundary checks exclude F₀ = 0 and F₁ = F₂ = 1, while correctly including the composite index 4 because F₄ = 3. Computed qualifying indices through 30 and their Fibonacci values agree with the source lists. The test theorem elaborates to the intended equivalence, and its existing proof has no sorryAx dependency. Wikipedia, MathWorld, and the cited paper describe infinitude as open, consistent with both research-open tags.
